strings.par2.redundancy_hint: How much extra data to generate. 5% is the usual choice: for large archives the set takes about that share, but for small ones it is noticeably bigger, because a set always consists of eight files.
strings.par2.block_auto_hint: Automatic picks the block size to suit the file size. It works well on large archives and poorly on small ones: measured on a 12 MiB archive it chose a 6 KiB block and the set came to 23.7% instead of 12%. On a small archive, set the block yourself.
strings.par2.block_manual_warning: A manual block size is not a drawback: on a 200 MiB archive a 512 KiB block gave a 12.1% set and built faster than automatic. Only a too-large block hurts — 4 MiB on a 12 MiB archive pushed the set to 33%. Rule of thumb: about 1 MiB per 1 MiB of file.
strings.par2.limits_note: The set is created next to the archive and protects the data itself: bad sectors, failed writes, corrupted transfers. It does not protect against loss of the medium — that needs a copy of the archive elsewhere. Creating a set reads the whole archive and may take several minutes.
strings.par2.create_skipped: Archive unchanged, set left in place
strings.par2.not_found: engine not found, set not created
strings.par2.repair_confirm_text:
The following file will be overwritten:
{name}

Size on disk: {actual} bytes
Set was made for: {recorded} bytes

Damaged parts will be rebuilt from the recovery data. This cannot be undone. Continue?
strings.par2.repair_stale: repair blocked: the set is stale — the archive does not match the set ({actual} bytes on disk, set covers {recorded}). Repair would roll the archive back to the set's version and overwrite the current file. Recreate the set first.
strings.par2.verify_unrepairable: archive damaged, not enough recovery data to repair it
strings.par2.verify_broken: recovery set is present but cannot be read
strings.par2.repair_impossible: restore not possible: the damage is too large for the recovery data
strings.par2.repair_not_needed: restore not needed: the archive and its set are intact
strings.par2.repair_no_size: restore blocked: could not read the size recorded in the set
strings.par2.intro: A PAR2 recovery set stores spare copies of the archive's fragments next to it. If part of the file is damaged — a bad sector, a failed write, an interrupted copy — the missing pieces can be rebuilt from the set, without the original data.

strings.par2.repair_confirm_same_size:
The file will be overwritten:
{name}

On disk: {actual} bytes
Set covers: {recorded} bytes

The sizes match but the contents differ. Either the file is damaged, or the set was made for a DIFFERENT version of an archive of the same size (for example, the archive was replaced by a newer backup).

Repair will restore the version FROM THE SET and overwrite the current file. If the set is stale, use "Recreate the set" instead. Continue?
